definition: The wake-sleep algorithm is an unsupervised learning algorithm for deep generative models, especially Helmholtz Machines.
details: The algorithm is similar to the expectation-maximization algorithm, and optimizes the model likelihood for observed data. The name of the algorithm derives from its use of two learning phases, the “wake” phase and the “sleep” phase, which are performed alternately. It can be conceived as a model for learning in the brain, but is also being applied for machine learning.
